text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Russian newspapers this morning. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
KOMMERSANT DAILY
- The government is planning to cut spending in order to meet revenue targets in the 1998 budget it will submit to the Duma shortly.
- An accident on the launch pad in Kazakhstan which slightly damaged a Russian spy satellite due to go into orbit tonight might have turned the sophisticated machine into a chunk of metal.
- The Russian Communications Ministry has cut off telephone lines to Chechnya, a move which enraged Russian security officials negotiating an oil deal with the separatist republic.
- Chechen officials have successfully played the oil card in tough haggling with Russia over the future of their region.
- Duma deputies expressed discontent with the results of privatisation but said it should continue.
- The World Bank gives the go-ahead to new credits to Russia.
- Tax authorities expect better cooperation from commercial banks.
- Kirishinefteorgsintez, one of Russia's biggest oil refineries, is launching a $1 billion investment programme.
- Russian oil giant Lukoil says it plans rapid expansion through foreign projects.
- Russian regions, desperately short of funds, are working to raise money abroad.
- Pallada-GTsB mutual fund is told to bring its capital up to 2.5 billion roubles or face the withdrawal of its licence.
SEVODNYA
- Oil drilling in Iraq could become for Russian companies a viable alternative to problem-riddled projects of Azeri oil transportation through rebel Chechnya.
- Alfred Kokh, head of State Property Committee, says his relations with State Duma have passed the stage of confrontation.
- The 1998 budget, discussed on Thursday, provides for better tax collection and lower spending.
- Commercial banks are failing to fulfil meet their obligataions on budget payments.
- Lukoil plans to acquire a number of oil companies in central Russia.
NEZAVISIMAYA GAZETA
- An oil deal between Russia and separatist Chechnya on Azeri oil transportation seems to be on the cards, but a lot of problems related to the project remain unresolved.
- The Duma gives low marks to Russian privatisation.
- Young reformers who have so far left the Central Bank out of their purges could now try to pull the rug from under Sergei Dubinin's feet.
- First Deputy Prime Minister Anatoly Chubais has virtually become hostage to any blunder that any member of his tight-knit teem could commit.
ROSSIISKIYE VESTI
- President Boris Yeltsin and his administration have opened an Internet website.
- The fate of the 1998 budget depends on whether the Duma adopts a new tax code before too long.
- The 1998 budget is likely to become the first in Russia's history to be realistic enough to be executed.
MOSKOVSKY KOMSOMOLETS
- Phone charges in Moscow will double by the end of the year.
- Moscow mayor Yuri Luzhkov orders a cut of one third in the car fleet of municipal officials.
--Andrei Shukshin, Moscow Newsroom, +7095 941 8520
